10th.name: 10th Level / LDC
10th.description: Common preliminary foundation for LDC and other posts accepting 10th-level qualifications. Build Kerala and Indian GK, science, arithmetic and mental ability.

bucketLabels.knowledge: General Knowledge, Current Affairs & Kerala Renaissance

10th.syllabusNote: The official 10th-level common preliminary syllabus allocates 60 marks to General Knowledge, Current Affairs and Renaissance in Kerala, 20 to General Science, and 20 to Simple Arithmetic and Mental Ability. Post-specific LDC tests may add other topics.

plus_two.name: Plus Two Level
plus_two.description: Common preliminary practice across history, geography, civics, economics, constitution, sciences, computer science, languages and aptitude.
plus_two.syllabusNote: The linked Kerala PSC Plus Two common preliminary syllabus shows the mark split used here. Check the notification for the post and exam cycle you are applying for.

degree.name: Degree Level
degree.description: Degree-level common preliminary foundation with larger shares for arithmetic, reasoning and English, plus general knowledge and language.
degree.syllabusNote: Based on the revised Degree Level Common Preliminary syllabus and mark distribution published by Kerala PSC in 2025. Check the current post notification for the official syllabus.

questions.question: The Vaikom Satyagraha began in which year?
questions.explanation: The Vaikom Satyagraha began in 1924 and challenged restrictions on access to roads around the Vaikom temple.

questions.question: The Temple Entry Proclamation of Travancore was issued in 1936 by whom?
questions.explanation: The proclamation was issued by the Travancore ruler Chithira Thirunal on 12 November 1936.

questions.question: Sree Narayana Guru's Aruvippuram consecration took place in which year?
questions.explanation: In 1888, Sree Narayana Guru consecrated a Shiva idol at Aruvippuram, a landmark in the Kerala renaissance.

questions.question: Who founded the Sadhu Jana Paripalana Sangham?
questions.explanation: Ayyankali organised the Sadhu Jana Paripalana Sangham to advance the rights and education of oppressed communities.

questions.question: The Sree Narayana Dharma Paripalana Yogam (SNDP Yogam) was established in which year?
questions.explanation: The SNDP Yogam was formed in 1903, drawing inspiration from Sree Narayana Guru's social reform work.

questions.question: Who founded the Nair Service Society (NSS)?
questions.explanation: Mannathu Padmanabhan founded the NSS in 1914 as a community organisation.

questions.question: Kerala state was formed on 1 November in which year?
questions.explanation: Kerala was formed on 1 November 1956 during the reorganisation of Indian states.

questions.question: The Malabar Rebellion took place in which year?
questions.explanation: The Malabar Rebellion occurred in 1921 in the Malabar region; study its causes and context alongside the freedom movement.

questions.question: Who wrote the Malayalam novel Indulekha?
questions.explanation: O. Chandu Menon's Indulekha, published in 1889, is widely recognised as the first major Malayalam novel.

questions.question: The Indian National Congress was founded in which year?
questions.explanation: The Indian National Congress was founded in 1885; its first session met in Bombay.

questions.question: Who presided over the first session of the Indian National Congress?
questions.explanation: W. C. Bonnerjee presided over the first INC session in Bombay in 1885.

questions.question: The Quit India Movement was launched in which year?
questions.explanation: The Quit India Movement was launched in August 1942, during the Second World War.

questions.question: Mahatma Gandhi's Salt March to Dandi took place in which year?
questions.explanation: Gandhi's Salt March began in March 1930 as a protest against the British salt laws.

questions.question: The uprising commonly called the Revolt of 1857 first spread from which garrison town?
questions.explanation: The large uprising of 1857 began at Meerut before spreading to other parts of north India.

questions.question: The French Revolution began in which year?
questions.explanation: The French Revolution began in 1789 and transformed France's political and social order.

questions.question: Who is associated with the slogan 'One caste, one religion, one God for humankind'?
questions.explanation: The slogan is associated with Sree Narayana Guru's message of social equality and human dignity.

questions.question: The first session of the Indian National Congress was held in which city?
questions.explanation: The first INC session was held in Bombay in December 1885.

questions.question: Pazhassi Raja is especially remembered for resisting which power in Malabar?
questions.explanation: Pazhassi Raja led resistance against the expanding authority of the British East India Company in Malabar.

questions.question: What is the highest peak in Kerala and peninsular India?
questions.explanation: Anamudi, in the Western Ghats, is the highest peak in Kerala and peninsular India.

questions.question: Which is the longest river that flows entirely within Kerala?
questions.explanation: The Periyar is Kerala's longest river; standard references give its length as about 244 km.

questions.question: Which is the largest lake in Kerala?
questions.explanation: Vembanad is the largest lake in Kerala and forms part of the state's extensive backwater system.

questions.question: Which sea lies to the west of Kerala?
questions.explanation: Kerala is on India's southwestern coast, facing the Arabian Sea.

questions.question: The Palakkad Gap is a low pass through which mountain range?
questions.explanation: The Palakkad Gap is a low pass in the Western Ghats that links central Kerala with the Coimbatore region.

questions.question: How many revenue districts does Kerala have?
questions.explanation: Kerala has 14 districts. Check official state sources for any future administrative changes.

questions.question: Kuttanad is well known for farming that takes place partly below what level?
questions.explanation: Parts of Kuttanad are cultivated below sea level, a distinctive feature of the region's farming system.

questions.question: Silent Valley National Park is in which Kerala district?
questions.explanation: Silent Valley National Park lies in Palakkad district and protects tropical evergreen forest in the Nilgiri region.

questions.question: What is the standard meridian of India?
questions.explanation: India's standard meridian is 82°30′ E, used to define Indian Standard Time.

questions.question: Which Indian state has the largest area?
questions.explanation: Rajasthan is India's largest state by area.

questions.question: The Western Ghats run broadly parallel to which Indian coastline?
questions.explanation: The Western Ghats extend roughly parallel to India's western coast.

questions.question: Which instrument records earthquake ground motion?
questions.explanation: A seismograph records ground motion generated by earthquakes; a seismogram is its recorded trace.

questions.question: What does GDP measure?

options.A: The value of final goods and services produced within an economy during a period
options.B: Only the government's annual tax collection
options.D: The total population of a country

questions.explanation: Gross Domestic Product measures the market value of final goods and services produced within a territory over a specified period.

questions.question: Inflation is best described as a sustained rise in what?
questions.explanation: Inflation is a sustained increase in the general price level, which reduces the purchasing power of money.

questions.question: Which institution is India's central bank?

options.C: Securities and Exchange Board of India
options.D: National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development

questions.explanation: The Reserve Bank of India is the country's central bank and conducts monetary policy.

questions.question: Which of these is a direct tax in India?
questions.explanation: Personal income tax is levied directly on the income of a taxpayer; GST and customs duty are indirect taxes.

questions.question: NITI Aayog replaced which institution in 2015?
questions.explanation: NITI Aayog was established in 2015 to replace the Planning Commission.

questions.question: The Goods and Services Tax was introduced across India on which date?
questions.explanation: GST was rolled out in India on 1 July 2017. Specific tax rules can change, so use current official material for updates.

questions.question: A government's fiscal policy mainly concerns decisions about what?
questions.explanation: Fiscal policy uses government revenue, taxation and expenditure to influence the economy.

questions.question: The repo rate is the rate at which which institution lends short-term funds to banks?

options.D: Comptroller and Auditor General of India

questions.explanation: The repo rate is the policy rate at which the RBI lends funds to eligible banks against approved securities.

questions.question: The Right to Information Act in India was enacted in which year?
questions.explanation: The Right to Information Act, 2005 provides a framework for citizens to request information from public authorities, subject to its provisions and exemptions.

questions.question: Who directly elects members of the Lok Sabha?
questions.explanation: Lok Sabha members are directly elected by voters in parliamentary constituencies.

questions.question: A Gram Sabha consists of which people?

options.A: People registered on the electoral rolls of the village panchayat area
options.C: All government employees in the district
options.D: Only the heads of village households

questions.explanation: The Gram Sabha is the body of registered voters in the area of a village panchayat, as defined by law.

questions.question: Which body conducts elections to Parliament and State Legislatures in India?

options.D: Comptroller and Auditor General of India

questions.explanation: The Election Commission of India supervises elections to Parliament, State Legislatures, and the offices of President and Vice-President.

questions.question: Public administration is primarily concerned with what?

options.A: Implementing public policies and delivering public services

questions.explanation: Public administration translates laws and public policies into programmes and services.

questions.question: A State Lokayukta institution is generally associated with investigating what?

options.A: Allegations of maladministration or corruption within its legal jurisdiction

questions.explanation: Lokayukta powers and procedures are defined by the relevant state law; the institution generally addresses complaints about public functionaries.

questions.question: Which is the highest court in India's judicial system?
questions.explanation: The Supreme Court of India is the apex court in the country's judicial hierarchy.

questions.question: E-governance uses information and communication technology mainly to improve what?

options.A: Access to and delivery of public services and information
options.B: The number of paper forms required

questions.explanation: E-governance uses digital systems to make public information and services more accessible and efficient.

questions.question: The Constitution of India was adopted on which date?
questions.explanation: The Constituent Assembly adopted the Constitution on 26 November 1949; it came into force on 26 January 1950.

questions.question: The Constitution of India came into force on which date?
questions.explanation: The Constitution came into force on 26 January 1950, celebrated as Republic Day.

questions.question: Fundamental Rights are primarily set out in which Part of the Constitution?
questions.explanation: Part III of the Constitution contains the Fundamental Rights.

questions.question: Directive Principles of State Policy are primarily contained in which Part?
questions.explanation: Part IV contains the Directive Principles of State Policy; they guide governance and are not enforceable by courts in the same way as Fundamental Rights.

questions.question: Fundamental Duties are listed in which Part of the Constitution?
questions.explanation: Fundamental Duties are set out in Part IVA; Article 51A was added by the 42nd Amendment.

questions.question: Article 14 guarantees which constitutional principle?

options.A: Equality before the law and equal protection of the laws
options.C: A right to property as a Fundamental Right
options.D: The procedure for amending the Constitution

questions.explanation: Article 14 guarantees equality before the law and equal protection of the laws.

questions.question: Article 21 protects which right?

options.A: Protection of life and personal liberty
options.B: The right to form a State
options.D: The procedure for passing a Money Bill

questions.explanation: Article 21 states that no person shall be deprived of life or personal liberty except according to procedure established by law.

questions.question: Article 32 is associated with which remedy?

options.A: The right to move the Supreme Court for enforcement of Fundamental Rights
options.C: The creation of a new district

questions.explanation: Article 32 provides the right to approach the Supreme Court for enforcement of Fundamental Rights.

questions.question: Which Schedule contains the Union, State and Concurrent Lists?
questions.explanation: The Seventh Schedule distributes legislative subjects across the Union, State and Concurrent Lists.

questions.question: Which Article sets out the constitutional amendment procedure?
questions.explanation: Article 368 provides the procedure for amending the Constitution, with requirements that vary by the amendment's subject.

questions.question: The 73rd Constitutional Amendment is primarily associated with which institution?
questions.explanation: The 73rd Amendment gave constitutional recognition to Panchayati Raj institutions.

questions.question: Which Article provides for a Finance Commission at the Union level?
questions.explanation: Article 280 provides for the constitution of a Finance Commission by the President, normally every five years or earlier.

questions.question: Kathakali is a traditional performing art associated with which state?
questions.explanation: Kathakali is a classical dance-drama tradition of Kerala, known for stylised gesture, music and elaborate make-up.

questions.question: Mohiniyattam is a classical dance form associated with which state?
questions.explanation: Mohiniyattam is a classical dance form that developed in Kerala.

questions.question: Who is credited with creating Ottan Thullal?
questions.explanation: Poet Kunchan Nambiar created Ottan Thullal, a Malayalam performance tradition using satire and verse.

questions.question: Who was a principal founder of Kerala Kalamandalam?
questions.explanation: Vallathol Narayana Menon was central to founding Kerala Kalamandalam in 1930 to support classical arts.

questions.question: Who was the first Malayalam-language recipient of the Jnanpith Award?
questions.explanation: G. Sankara Kurup received the first Jnanpith Award for Malayalam in 1965.

questions.question: Who wrote the novel Chemmeen?
questions.explanation: Chemmeen is a celebrated Malayalam novel by Thakazhi Sivasankara Pillai.

questions.question: Who wrote Balyakalasakhi?
questions.explanation: Balyakalasakhi is a well-known Malayalam novel by Vaikom Muhammad Basheer.

questions.question: The traditional ritual art form Theyyam is especially associated with which part of Kerala?

options.C: The high ranges of Idukki only

questions.explanation: Theyyam is a ritual performance tradition especially associated with North Malabar in Kerala.

questions.question: Kalaripayattu is best described as what?

options.A: A traditional martial art of Kerala

questions.explanation: Kalaripayattu is a traditional martial art associated with Kerala.

questions.question: Onam celebrations are traditionally linked in Kerala folklore with the return of which king?
questions.explanation: Onam is linked in Kerala folklore with the annual return of the benevolent king Mahabali, also called Maveli.

questions.question: Vallam Kali refers to which activity?
questions.explanation: Vallam Kali is the traditional boat-racing culture of Kerala, including the famous snake-boat races.

questions.question: Koodiyattam is a traditional form of which theatre?
questions.explanation: Koodiyattam is a Sanskrit theatre tradition of Kerala recognised by UNESCO as intangible cultural heritage.

questions.question: The Jnanpith Award recognises outstanding contributions to which field?
questions.explanation: The Jnanpith Award is a major Indian literary award.

questions.question: Major Dhyan Chand is especially remembered for excellence in which sport?
questions.explanation: Major Dhyan Chand was an iconic Indian field-hockey player, often called the Wizard of Hockey.

questions.question: Who became the first Indian to win an individual Olympic gold medal?
questions.explanation: Abhinav Bindra won India's first individual Olympic gold medal in the men's 10-metre air rifle event at Beijing 2008.

questions.question: How many players from one team are on the field in association football under the standard Laws of the Game?
questions.explanation: A standard association-football team has eleven players on the field, including the goalkeeper.

questions.question: The Olympic symbol consists of how many interlaced rings?
questions.explanation: The Olympic symbol has five interlaced rings representing the union of the Olympic movement's continents; the colours are not assigned one-to-one to continents.

questions.question: The first modern Olympic Games were held in which city in 1896?
questions.explanation: The first modern Olympic Games were held in Athens in 1896.

questions.question: What is the next number in the series 3, 6, 12, 24, ___?
questions.explanation: Each term is doubled: 24 × 2 = 48.

questions.question: Complete the number analogy: 3 is to 9 as 5 is to ___.
questions.explanation: The first number is squared: 3² = 9, so 5² = 25.
questions.mnemonic: Look for the same operation on both sides: 3 × 3, then 5 × 5.

questions.question: Maya is Nikhil's sister. Nikhil is Anu's father. How is Maya related to Anu?
questions.explanation: Maya is the sister of Anu's father, so Maya is Anu's paternal aunt.

questions.question: A person faces north, turns right, then turns right again. Which direction are they facing?
questions.explanation: A right turn from north faces east; a second right turn faces south.

questions.question: What is the smaller angle between the clock hands at exactly 3 o'clock?
questions.explanation: At 3:00 the minute hand is at 12 and the hour hand at 3; the smaller angle is one quarter turn, or 90 degrees.

questions.question: In a row, Ravi is 8th from the left and 10th from the right. How many people are in the row?
questions.explanation: Total people = position from left + position from right − 1 = 8 + 10 − 1 = 17.
questions.mnemonic: L + R − 1: the person in the middle was counted from both ends.

questions.question: If today is Monday, what day of the week will it be 10 days later?
questions.explanation: Ten days is one week plus three days. Three days after Monday is Thursday.
questions.mnemonic: For weekday questions, remove full groups of 7 first; only count the remainder.

questions.question: Which name comes first in alphabetical order?
questions.explanation: Compare the first letters: A comes before B and M; among Anil and Arun, 'n' comes before 'r'.

questions.question: What is 3/4 of 80?
questions.explanation: Divide 80 by 4 to get 20, then multiply by 3: 20 × 3 = 60.
questions.mnemonic: For 'fraction of', divide by the bottom, then multiply by the top.

questions.question: Deficiency of vitamin C can cause which disease?
questions.explanation: Vitamin C deficiency causes scurvy; citrus fruits and several vegetables are dietary sources.

questions.question: Deficiency of vitamin D in children can cause which condition?
questions.explanation: Vitamin D is needed for healthy bone mineralisation; prolonged deficiency in children can cause rickets.

questions.question: Which protein in red blood cells carries most of the oxygen in blood?
questions.explanation: Haemoglobin in red blood cells binds and transports most oxygen in the blood.

questions.question: Which organ produces insulin?
questions.explanation: Insulin is produced by beta cells in the pancreas and helps regulate blood glucose.

questions.question: Which organs filter blood and produce urine?
questions.explanation: The kidneys filter blood, regulate water and salts, and produce urine.

questions.question: Which pigment captures much of the light energy used in photosynthesis?
questions.explanation: Chlorophyll in plant chloroplasts absorbs light used to drive photosynthesis.

questions.question: Which gas do green plants take in from the air for photosynthesis?
questions.explanation: Plants use carbon dioxide and water to make sugars during photosynthesis, releasing oxygen.

questions.question: How many chambers does a typical human heart have?
questions.explanation: The human heart has two atria and two ventricles, making four chambers.

questions.question: Tuberculosis is caused by which organism?
questions.explanation: Tuberculosis is caused by bacteria in the Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex and mainly affects the lungs.

questions.question: Malaria parasites are commonly transmitted to humans by which mosquito?
questions.explanation: Female Anopheles mosquitoes transmit malaria parasites when they feed on human blood.

questions.question: What is the largest organ of the human body by surface area?
questions.explanation: Skin is the body's largest organ by surface area and forms an important protective barrier.

questions.question: How many chromosomes are normally present in most human body cells?
questions.explanation: Most human somatic cells have 46 chromosomes arranged in 23 pairs.

questions.question: Vaccines primarily help the immune system to do what?

options.A: Recognise a pathogen and respond more effectively in the future
options.C: Remove the need for clean water

questions.explanation: Vaccines train immune responses against particular pathogens; protection varies by vaccine and disease.

questions.question: Which organisms are especially important in decomposing dead organic matter?
questions.explanation: Many bacteria and fungi break down dead organic matter and return nutrients to ecosystems.

questions.question: What is the SI unit of force?
questions.explanation: The newton (N) is the SI unit of force.

questions.question: What is the SI unit of electric current?
questions.explanation: Electric current is measured in amperes (A).

questions.question: Average speed is calculated using which relationship?

options.A: Distance travelled divided by time taken

questions.explanation: Average speed equals total distance travelled divided by total time taken.

questions.question: Why does sound not travel through a perfect vacuum?

options.A: It needs a material medium to carry vibrations
options.B: Sound is made only of light
options.C: A vacuum is too cold for sound

questions.explanation: Sound is a mechanical wave, so it needs matter to transmit vibrations.

questions.question: For reflection from a plane mirror, the angle of incidence is equal to what?

options.B: The angle of refraction in every material

questions.explanation: The law of reflection states that the angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection.

questions.question: What is the SI base unit of thermodynamic temperature?
questions.explanation: The kelvin (K) is the SI base unit of thermodynamic temperature.

questions.question: What is the SI unit of work and energy?
questions.explanation: The joule (J) is the SI unit of both work and energy.

questions.question: At standard conditions, a solution with pH 7 is described as what?
questions.explanation: A pH of 7 is neutral at 25 °C; lower values are acidic and higher values are basic.

questions.question: What is the atomic number of oxygen?
questions.explanation: Oxygen has atomic number 8, meaning its nucleus contains eight protons.

questions.question: What is the chemical formula of water?
questions.explanation: A water molecule contains two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom, written H₂O.

questions.question: Ordinary rusting of iron requires iron, oxygen and the presence of what?
questions.explanation: Rusting is an oxidation process that normally requires both oxygen and moisture.

questions.question: What is the SI unit of power?
questions.explanation: Power is the rate of doing work or transferring energy; its SI unit is the watt.

questions.question: What colour does blue litmus generally turn in an acidic solution?
questions.explanation: Acids turn blue litmus red; indicators are a simple way to test acidic solutions.

questions.question: What is the approximate acceleration due to gravity near Earth's surface?
questions.explanation: The standard value of gravitational acceleration near Earth's surface is about 9.8 m/s²; it varies slightly by location.

questions.question: Which Indian organisation is responsible for the national space programme?

options.B: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India

questions.explanation: ISRO is India's national space agency and conducts the country's space programme.

questions.question: Which launch vehicle family is used by India to place heavier payloads into orbit?
questions.explanation: LVM3 is ISRO's heavy-lift launch vehicle family. Specific mission configurations and capabilities evolve over time.

questions.question: Where is the headquarters of the Indian Space Research Organisation?
questions.explanation: ISRO's headquarters is in Bengaluru, Karnataka.

questions.question: Which type of electromagnetic radiation is commonly used in remote controls?
questions.explanation: Many television and appliance remotes transmit control signals using infrared light.

questions.question: Which gas is the main contributor to human-caused global warming?
questions.explanation: Carbon dioxide is the largest contributor to human-caused warming among long-lived greenhouse gases, though other gases also matter.

questions.question: A photovoltaic solar cell converts sunlight directly into what?
questions.explanation: Photovoltaic cells convert light directly into electrical energy through the photovoltaic effect.

questions.question: In a controlled experiment, why is one variable changed at a time when practical?

options.A: To help identify the effect of that variable
options.C: To guarantee every hypothesis is true
options.D: To remove the need for repeated trials

questions.explanation: Changing one factor while controlling others helps researchers identify which factor caused an observed effect.

questions.question: Which instrument is used to measure atmospheric pressure?
questions.explanation: A barometer measures atmospheric pressure.

questions.question: Which computer component executes instructions and performs calculations?
questions.explanation: The CPU processes instructions and coordinates many of a computer's operations.

questions.question: Which kind of memory normally loses its contents when power is switched off?
questions.explanation: RAM is volatile working memory; its contents are normally lost when power is removed.

questions.question: A keyboard is primarily which type of device?
questions.explanation: A keyboard sends text and commands to a computer, so it is an input device.

questions.question: Which is a non-volatile storage device?
questions.explanation: An SSD keeps stored data when power is off and is used for persistent storage.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of a web browser?

options.A: To retrieve and display web pages
options.B: To physically connect a computer to electricity

questions.explanation: A browser requests web resources and displays pages; a search engine helps locate pages.

questions.question: What is phishing?

options.A: A deceptive attempt to obtain sensitive information by impersonation
options.B: A method of safely backing up files

questions.explanation: Phishing messages imitate trusted sources to trick people into revealing passwords or financial information.

questions.question: A Local Area Network (LAN) usually connects devices across what scale?

options.A: A limited local area such as a room, office or building

questions.explanation: A LAN connects devices in a relatively small area, such as a home, school or office.

questions.question: Which software manages computer hardware and provides services for applications?
questions.explanation: An operating system manages hardware resources and provides common services for applications.

questions.question: What does HTTPS indicate about a web connection?

options.A: The connection uses encrypted transport between the browser and site
options.B: The website is guaranteed to be honest
options.D: The internet is working without any server

questions.explanation: HTTPS uses TLS to protect data in transit; it does not guarantee that a site itself is trustworthy.

questions.question: Which application is best suited to calculations arranged in rows and columns?
questions.explanation: Spreadsheet applications organise data in cells and provide formulas, tables and charts.

questions.question: Choose the correct verb: 'Each of the students ___ submitted the form.'
questions.explanation: 'Each' is singular, so it takes the singular verb 'has'.

questions.question: Choose the correct verb: 'Neither Ravi nor Rani ___ present today.'
questions.explanation: With 'neither...nor', the verb generally agrees with the nearer subject; here 'Rani' is singular.

questions.question: Choose the correct article: 'She is ___ honest officer.'
questions.explanation: 'Honest' begins with a vowel sound because its 'h' is silent, so 'an' is used.

questions.question: Choose the correct word: 'I have lived here ___ 2020.'
questions.explanation: Use 'since' with the starting point of a period; use 'for' with its duration.

questions.question: Complete the second conditional: 'If I ___ more time, I would help.'
questions.explanation: A second conditional uses a past-form verb in the if-clause and 'would' in the result clause.

questions.question: Choose the correct comparative form of 'good'.
questions.explanation: 'Good' is irregular: good, better, best.

questions.question: Choose the passive form of 'They have completed the task.'

options.A: The task has been completed by them.
options.C: They were completed by the task.

questions.explanation: In the present perfect passive, use 'has/have been' plus the past participle.

questions.question: In reported speech, 'He said, “I am tired”' becomes which sentence?

options.A: He said that he was tired.
options.B: He said that I am tired.
options.D: He said that he is tiring.

questions.explanation: When the reporting verb is in the past, the present tense commonly shifts back: 'am' becomes 'was'.

questions.question: What does the phrasal verb 'look after' mean?
questions.explanation: 'Look after' means to care for or be responsible for someone or something.

questions.question: Choose the closest synonym of 'abundant'.
questions.explanation: 'Abundant' means existing in large quantities; 'plentiful' is a close synonym.

questions.question: Choose the antonym of 'scarce'.
questions.explanation: 'Scarce' means in short supply; 'plentiful' means available in abundance.

questions.question: What is the plural form of 'criterion'?
questions.explanation: 'Criterion' is a Greek-derived noun; its plural form is 'criteria'.

questions.question: Which collective noun commonly describes a group of birds?
questions.explanation: A group of birds is commonly called a flock.

questions.question: Which spelling is correct?
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'accommodation', with two c's and two m's.

questions.question: What is a person who compiles dictionaries called?
questions.explanation: A lexicographer writes or edits dictionaries.

questions.question: What does the idiom 'break the ice' usually mean?

options.A: To make people feel more relaxed at the start of an interaction

questions.explanation: 'Break the ice' means to ease tension or begin friendly conversation in a social situation.

questions.question: Which prefix changes 'possible' to its opposite?
questions.explanation: The prefix 'im-' forms 'impossible', meaning not possible.

questions.question: Choose the correct form: 'She enjoys ___ novels.'
questions.explanation: The verb 'enjoy' is normally followed by a gerund, so 'reading' is correct.

questions.question: Choose the correct pronoun: 'The secret is between you and ___.'
questions.explanation: The preposition 'between' takes the objective pronoun 'me'.

questions.question: In 'The child spoke softly', which word is the adverb?
questions.explanation: 'Softly' modifies the verb 'spoke' and tells how the child spoke, so it is an adverb.

questions.question: Choose the future perfect form: 'By Friday, we ___ the project.'
questions.explanation: The future perfect uses 'will have' followed by the past participle.

questions.question: Choose the correct phrase: '___ the heavy rain, the match continued.'
questions.explanation: 'In spite of' is followed by a noun phrase; 'despite' is used without 'of'.

questions.question: Complete the pair: 'Neither the teacher ___ the students were late.'
questions.explanation: The standard correlative pair is 'neither...nor'.

questions.question: Choose the correct verb: 'A number of applicants ___ waiting outside.'
questions.explanation: 'A number of' means several and normally takes a plural verb.

questions.question: Which sentence uses 'advice' correctly?

options.A: She gave me some useful advice.

questions.explanation: 'Advice' is normally an uncountable noun in standard English; say 'some advice' or 'a piece of advice'.

questions.question: What does the word 'benevolent' mean?
questions.explanation: 'Benevolent' describes a person or action that is kind and well-meaning.

questions.question: ‘സന്തോഷം’ എന്ന പദത്തിന്റെ പര്യായം ഏത്?
questions.explanation: ‘സന്തോഷം’ എന്നതിന് അടുത്ത അർത്ഥമുള്ള പദമാണ് ‘ആനന്ദം’.

questions.question: ‘ഉയരം’ എന്ന പദത്തിന്റെ വിപരീതപദം ഏത്?
questions.explanation: ‘ഉയരം’ എന്നതിന്റെ വിപരീത അർത്ഥം ‘താഴ്ച’ എന്നാണ്.

questions.question: ‘വനം’ എന്ന പദത്തിന്റെ പര്യായം ഏത്?
questions.explanation: ‘വനം’ എന്നതിന് സമാനമായ പദമാണ് ‘കാട്’.

questions.question: ‘പ്രകാശം’ എന്ന പദത്തിന്റെ വിപരീതം ഏത്?
questions.explanation: ‘പ്രകാശം’ എന്നതിന്റെ വിപരീതപദമാണ് ‘ഇരുട്ട്’.

questions.question: ‘പുതിയത്’ എന്ന പദത്തിന്റെ വിപരീതം ഏത്?
questions.explanation: ‘പുതിയത്’ എന്നതിന്റെ വിപരീത അർത്ഥമുള്ള പദമാണ് ‘പഴയത്’.

questions.question: ‘മരം’ എന്ന പദത്തിന്റെ ബഹുവചനം ഏത്?
questions.explanation: ‘മരം’ എന്ന നാമത്തിന്റെ സാധാരണ ബഹുവചനരൂപമാണ് ‘മരങ്ങൾ’.

questions.question: ‘ജലം’ എന്ന പദത്തിന് സമാനമായ പദം ഏത്?
questions.explanation: ‘ജലം’ എന്ന സംസ്കൃതപദത്തിന് മലയാളത്തിലെ സാധാരണ സമാനപദമാണ് ‘വെള്ളം’.

questions.question: ‘സുന്ദരം’ എന്ന പദത്തിന്റെ പര്യായം ഏത്?
questions.explanation: ‘സുന്ദരം’ എന്നും ‘മനോഹരം’ എന്നും മനോഹാരിതയെ സൂചിപ്പിക്കുന്നു.

questions.question: ‘വിജയം’ എന്ന പദത്തിന്റെ വിപരീതം ഏത്?
questions.explanation: ‘വിജയം’ എന്നതിന്റെ വിപരീതപദമാണ് ‘പരാജയം’.

questions.question: ‘അധ്യാപകൻ’ എന്നതിന്റെ സ്ത്രീലിംഗരൂപം ഏത്?
questions.explanation: ‘അധ്യാപകൻ’ എന്ന പദത്തിന്റെ സ്ത്രീലിംഗരൂപമാണ് ‘അധ്യാപിക’.

questions.question: ‘സുഹൃത്ത്’ എന്ന പദത്തിന്റെ പര്യായം ഏത്?
questions.explanation: ‘സുഹൃത്ത്’ എന്നതിന് സമാനമായ പദമാണ് ‘മിത്രം’.

questions.question: ‘വലുത്’ എന്ന പദത്തിന്റെ വിപരീതം ഏത്?
questions.explanation: ‘വലുത്’ എന്നതിന്റെ വിപരീത അർത്ഥമുള്ള പദമാണ് ‘ചെറുത്’.
